minimumClosure: Process exercised before 1.0 or public beta as applicable

gates.evidence: Versioned pre-1.0 support policy defines main/active-candidate supported lines and severity-specific security-fix behavior; drill proves the active version remains writable and known-bad version is separately blocked.
Executable vulnerability lifecycle runs RECEIVED→TRIAGED→EMBARGOED→FIX_READY→ADVISORY_READY→DISCLOSED for critical/high while explicitly preserving the separate missing-private-channel boundary.
Incident policy assigns coordinator, security, release, storage and communications roles; every disaster drill records the role set and required containment/recovery actions.

Revocation policy freezes promotion, marks known-bad releases, conditionally deprecates/yanks published artifacts, invalidates release notices, publishes warnings and rebuilds clean provenance; publication actions remain conditional until artifacts actually exist.
Known-bad runtime drill applies VFS read-only mode with a version-bound reason; mutation fails while existing project reads and portable export remain allowed.
Dependency maintenance is exercised through npm audit on every CI plus weekly/monthly update policy and same-day high/critical triage; current security court remains zero-blocker.

Browser regression watch freezes OPFS/Web Locks/Service Worker/SharedArrayBuffer/crossOriginIsolated primitives and a weekly maintenance workflow reruns profile + 2-iteration installed-distribution browser court without central telemetry.
Telemetry-free local health receipt reports runtime/profile, browser primitives, workspace read-only/generation and diagnostics with remoteRequestCount=0 and centralServiceRequired=false.

Support bundle authority now exposes a backward parser for opencontainer.support-bundle.v0.1 and v0.2, rejects unknown schemas and unsafe privacy flags, and current diagnostics remain reproducible/privacy-minimized.
Backup/export policy explicitly calls browser storage best-effort, recommends portable export before risky events for important projects, and forbids nagging/false durability guarantees.
EOL disposition preserves project readability and portable export, blocks/read-only unsafe mutation and forbids destructive storage downgrade.
Issue-to-regression rule mechanically verifies all retained critical/high security fixes have stable IDs, executable tests and FIXED_RETAINED evidence; #413 checked 12 entries.
Known-issues database contains version/profile/browser mapping and only safe-or-null workarounds; #413 validated four current evidence/external gaps.

CI #413 executes four disaster drills—bad release rollback, corrupt workspace recovery, compromised publishing credential and browser primitive regression—with containment, recovery, notification, evidence preservation and post-incident regression.

boundaries: P17 process closure is pre-1.0 exercised-process evidence, not proof of a staffed 24x7 hosted operations organization.
The vulnerability workflow does not create or verify a private intake channel; P12-17 remains open.
Revocation/yank actions are simulated and conditional because no externally published npm/GitHub Release identity is claimed.
Weekly browser watch uses the declared Chrome profile; it does not close cross-browser, browser-floor or weak-device gates.
